Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray shows a markedly smaller and hyperlucent right hemithorax with diminished vascular markings, indicative of oligemia. Combined with the patient's history of Takayasu arteritis (a large-vessel vasculitis) and the CT finding of calcification/stenosis at the pulmonary artery origin, this appearance is characteristic of chronic obstruction of the right pulmonary artery leading to hypoplasia and reduced blood flow.
